subject.name: CBGB & OMFUG
subject.poc_goal: Build a provenance-first, time-versioned historical digital twin from reusable visual assets, public metadata, archival references, verified geometry and permissioned current capture.

rights_classes.A: Owned or newly captured by the project; preferred for commercial reconstruction.
rights_classes.B: Partner supplied with explicit commercial derivative/model-training rights.
rights_classes.C: Open/public-domain material; usable only under the exact item license and attribution/share-alike obligations.
rights_classes.D: Reference-only evidence. Store metadata, observations and links; do not copy into reconstruction training, textures or redistributed media without permission.
rights_classes.E: Restricted/prohibited source for derivative reconstruction. Do not scrape, bypass controls, download contrary to terms, train on, or derive production geometry/textures from it.

source_groups.title: The Bowery Historic District - National Register of Historic Places registration report
observations: 313-315 Bowery consists of two 1878 tenements joined and substantially altered in 1934 into a four-story four-bay lodging house with a modest Art Deco facade.
Hilly Kristal began leasing the Palace Bar ground-floor space in 1969, retained the old bar and many existing fixtures, and returned in 1973 under the CBGB name.
CBGB closed in 2006 and the National Register narrative states the club interior was largely preserved by the post-closure retail tenant.
The report cites an unpublished July 24, 2006 Historical documentation of 313-315 Bowery letter report by Lisa Kersavage and Marci Reaven as a key underlying source.

source_groups.title: NIGHTCLUBBING Archive by Pat Ivers and Emily Armstrong, MSS.305
observations: Collection includes 161 U-matic tapes, 24 Betacam tapes, 26 half-inch reels and 21 MiniDV items, with bulk dates 1975-1980.

Specific CBGB items include Dead Boys (Oct 1977), multiple May 1978 Blitz Benefit reels, Voidoids/Destroy All Monsters/Only Ones/Revelons (1979), Bad Brains (Dec 1979), Pin-ups and Student Teachers (Feb 1980), among others.
NYU states copyright/publicity/privacy rights were not transferred; permission to use materials must be secured from the copyright holder.

source_groups.title: Cornell Punk Flyers Collection
observations: Collection contains thousands of flyer records and includes CBGB-specific items.

Examples include Television and The Stilettos on May 5, 1974 at 315 Bowery and later flyers cataloged with 317 Bowery; address variants must remain observations rather than silently changing canonical geometry.
Cornell collection materials require item-level copyright assessment and are not commercial reconstruction inputs by default.

prohibited_or_reference_only_rules.rule: Do not scrape or create production 3D derived assets from Google imagery. Use it only to the extent its terms permit normal viewing/navigation, and replace missing geometry with owned/open/partner capture.

prohibited_or_reference_only_rules.source: Unlicensed social-media, press, commercial photography, documentary video, YouTube/Vimeo uploads
prohibited_or_reference_only_rules.rule: Store URLs, dates, creators, observations and human-created geometry notes only until derivative/commercial permission is documented. Do not download or train the production reconstruction from the media merely because it is publicly viewable.

Keep source-derived outputs isolated and record derivation. Review share-alike obligations before combining their pixels into a proprietary production texture/model. Prefer project-owned, CC BY or public-domain assets where practical.

collection_rule: Collect every discoverable digital footprint as metadata and evidence, but only copy/reconstruct from media whose rights permit the exact intended use. Every produced geometric or visual assertion must retain evidence IDs, time validity and confidence.
